headline: Medium risk: shared file-based workflows can leak or corrupt data, while OCR outputs may cascade into unverified downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations can read and write validation files, and PaddleOCR can process documents into outputs that may be copied into those files. No shared channel is documented, so prompt injection is only plausible through manual file handoff or pasted content, which is a limited pathway. The pair lacks evidence of permissive instruction parsing.
conditions: IF an operator copies PaddleOCR text output into Great Expectations documentation or config files without review, injected instructions can be introduced.
IF either agent is wired to consume the other's file output as trusted text, the pathway becomes active.
mitigations: Review any OCR-derived text before placing it into Great Expectations artifacts.
Keep OCR outputs in a separate staging folder from validation configs.
Use a fixed template for Great Expectations files and reject unexpected prose.
Disable copy-paste from untrusted OCR results into operational docs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to OCR outputs before downstream use.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations touches data sources, validation results, and documentation, while PaddleOCR handles documents and images and has allowlisted network egress. A shared workspace or file exchange could expose sensitive document contents to the OCR side and then out through its API calls. The profiles do not prove a default leak, but the interaction is plausible in common file-based workflows.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or document set, document contents can flow from Great Expectations into PaddleOCR.
IF PaddleOCR sends processed content to an external API, those documents may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate sensitive datasets from OCR input folders.
Run PaddleOCR only on redacted copies of documents.
Restrict network egress to a test endpoint during review.
Delete temporary OCR artifacts after each run.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation between validation and OCR jobs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations can install packages and write files, while PaddleOCR can run browsers and has allowlisted egress. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource or shared locking, so direct capability conflict is not established. Uncertainty remains because shared filesystem or orchestration details are absent, so the safer low severity is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same directory or git working tree, file conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator gives both agents mutable access to one shared resource without locks, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories to each agent.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared git state.
Serialize jobs that modify the same files.
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations produces validation results and documentation, and PaddleOCR can turn documents into structured outputs that downstream systems may trust. If PaddleOCR output is fed into Great Expectations or vice versa without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect validation or document processing. The pair lacks direct evidence of an automated trust chain, so medium fits the inferred default workflow risk.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is used as input to Great Expectations checks without human review, OCR mistakes can propagate.
IF Great Expectations validation results are treated as authoritative by a downstream document workflow, false confidence can spread.
mitigations: Require human review of OCR outputs before validation.
Compare OCR results against source documents for a sample set.
Flag low-confidence OCR fields for manual correction.
Keep validation failures visible in a separate report.
requires-engineering: add schema and confidence checks between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation, while PaddleOCR processes documents and images with allowlisted egress. The profiles do not show regulated data classes like PHI or EU PII, nor residency or certification mismatches, so compliance risk is limited to generic handling gaps. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is not documented, low severity is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF regulated documents are introduced into the OCR workflow, residency or retention mismatches may matter.
IF validation artifacts contain sensitive data and are retained longer than source documents, policy drift can occur.
mitigations: Classify documents before OCR processing.
Avoid sending regulated documents to external APIs.
Set a short retention window for OCR artifacts.
Document where validation results are stored and for how long.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies across both workflows.
